state.case_summary:
A 38-year-old woman presented with 4 months of progressively worsening symmetric pain in the small joints of her hands, wrists, knees, and ankles. She reported early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily and severe fatigue throughout the day. One month before presentation, she had a mild COVID-19 infection confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR; symptoms were limited to fever, chills, and a non-oxygen-requiring cough. She had not been vaccinated against COVID-19 at that time. She denied fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, rash, or appetite changes since recovering. There were no recent genitourinary or gastrointestinal infections and no history of psoriasis or uveitis. She is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol, and has no recreational drug use. Family history is notable for a maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis.

Laboratory studies showed an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 13 mm/hour and a C-reactive protein of 4.3 mg/L (both within normal limits). Immunologic testing revealed an antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640, negative extractable nuclear antigen and double-stranded DNA antibodies, a rheumatoid factor of 62.29 IU/mL (normal <20 IU/mL), and an anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody of 237.39 units (normal <20 units). Hepatitis B and C serologies were negative.

Radiographs of the hands, knees, ankles, and feet were unremarkable. Hand ultrasound showed no joint erosion. MRI of the hands demonstrated synovitis of the bilateral distal radioulnar joints and the left second metacarpophalangeal joint, with tenosynovitis around the extensor carpi ulnaris tendon; no osseous destruction was identified.

supporting_facts: symmetric pain in small joints of hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
excluded_candidates: Sjögren's syndrome: less likely due to lack of eye and mouth symptoms
Psoriatic arthritis: less likely due to lack of psoriasis history
Lupus: less likely due to negative double-stranded DNA antibodies and lack of systemic symptoms
Osteoarthritis: less likely due to symmetric joint involvement and presence of systemic fatigue
